next_guide.basis: Revenue/billings guide was raised in May and August, Q2 beat the top of guidance by ~$30m and Jefferies' field checks put calendar Q3 slightly above company forecasts, so a revenue raise is the base case; the EPS range was only narrowed last time and the largest EBA renewal cohort sits in Q4, so an EPS/FCF guide held flat is the main risk, plus any first FY28 framework without the transaction-model lift.

findings.finding: Earnings Whispers carries a whisper EPS of $3.16 against consensus $3.07 and the company's guide of $3.04-3.09, so the market bar sits ~2% above the top of guidance; a Q2-sized beat (EPS +5.8%, $3.30 vs $3.12) clears it, a smaller beat does not.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 and Q2 FY27 both beat EPS and revenue above guidance and fell -4.0% and -3.67%; Q3 FY26 beat and rose +2.36%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is the bar, not an unpriced fact; filed because it says a guide-top beat is already expected. If the market expected only an in-line print, the whisper would sit at or below consensus.
findings.independence: Jefferies (2026-11-09) also expects results without major surprises, which supports a beat being the base case (https://www.optionfinance.fr/info-financiere-en-continu/d/2026-11-09-jefferies-releve-son-objectif-de-cours-sur-autodesk.html).

findings.finding: The stock went into the print about 25% above its Sep 9 low of $206.62 (now $258.57, 20d +6.8%), after a 16.6% fall in eight sessions following the Q2 beat-and-raise; part of a good Q3 is now in the price, though it is still ~17% below its 52w high and down ~12-14% YTD against SPY +6.7%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY27 went in after a run and sold off 3.67% on the window, then 16.6% more over eight days.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is the price itself; what it changes is the bar. Had the market been left skeptical, the stock would sit near the September low with a heavy put skew; it sits 25% higher with a skew of only +1.88.
findings.independence: Jefferies notes ~25% rise since the quarter began (https://www.optionfinance.fr/info-financiere-en-continu/d/2026-11-09-jefferies-releve-son-objectif-de-cours-sur-autodesk.html); baseline 20d +6.8%.

findings.finding: The last two prints (May and August 2026) beat revenue and EPS above the top of guidance and raised revenue guidance, yet fell -4.0% and -3.67% because the full-year EPS guide stayed at or below street ($12.52-12.60 vs $12.60) and margin guidance was held at ~39%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS guide below street: -3.67% (Aug 2026), -4.0% (May 2026). EPS guide not an issue: +5.32% (Feb 2026), +2.36% (Nov 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: A reaction pattern, not a fact the market lacks; it tells the judges that a revenue beat-and-raise alone has not been bought this year. If the market had learned it, the whisper would not sit above the guide.
findings.independence: SiliconANGLE 2026-08-27: shares -5% after hours as cash-flow guidance narrowed (https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/27/autodesk-shares-fall-despite-q2-beat-as-cash-flow-guidance-narrows/); baseline history.

findings.finding: Jefferies (Nov 9) raised its target to $325 from $300 and said its field checks show calendar-Q3 activity slightly above the company's forecasts, with growth steady into 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Above-guide quarters were sold twice in 2026 (-4.0%, -3.67%) and bought in Nov 2025 (+2.36%).
findings.why_not_priced: A published sell-side check is partly priced (stock +25% since); what is not priced is the size: 'slightly above company forecasts' fits the whisper rather than beating it. Snippet_only: the page answered 403.
findings.independence: Procore's Q3 above-guide bookings (https://finviz.com/news/415677/procore-beats-as-organic-growth-accelerates-for-a-third-straight-quarter-but-the-dronedeploy-deal-changes-the-balance-sheet) point the same way on construction.

findings.finding: Loop Capital upgraded ADSK from Hold to Buy on 2026-11-13 (close $264.43); Fintel mean target $318.06.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline history on analyst actions; the stock fell 3.88% on Nov 17, two sessions after the upgrade (AAII).
findings.why_not_priced: Public and largely priced; filed because a pre-print upgrade marks sentiment going in. Snippet_only (page 503).
findings.independence: Jefferies target raise 2026-11-09 (shared sentiment, different firm).

findings.finding: Procore (Q3 reported Nov 3, covering Jul-Sep) grew revenue 19% to $402m against a $382-384m guide, raised full-year revenue by ~$21m organically, cited stronger bookings, and called the construction environment unchanged from the prior quarter; organic growth accelerated for a third quarter and the stock rose 11%.
findings.link: Direct competitor in construction management software: Autodesk Construction Cloud vs Procore; Autodesk's construction business grows 'north of 20%' (Q2 call); same customers (GCs, owners), same quarter (Procore Jul-Sep vs ADSK Aug-Oct, two overlapping months).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Construction >20% was a supporting line in the Q2 beat that was sold (-3.67%).
findings.why_not_priced: Peer read-through three weeks old and partly in ADSK's November high ($279); not in the ADSK consensus, which sits at the guide midpoint. Construction is a minority of ADSK revenue, so the net read is smaller than Procore's own beat.
findings.independence: Bentley (infrastructure) and Trimble AECO ARR +13% (separate documents) point the same way; AIA billings point the other way.

findings.finding: Bentley Systems (Q3 reported Nov 5) grew ARR 13% in constant currency, raised its full-year ARR growth outlook to 12.5-13.5%, and reported net revenue retention of 110%, a historical high.
findings.link: Infrastructure design software (OpenRoads/MicroStation vs Civil 3D/AutoCAD), shared civil engineering and infrastructure customers within ADSK's AECO line (~half of ADSK revenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not specific; AECO revenue +17% in Q2 FY27.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer signal on infrastructure demand; partly priced. If the market doubted AECO demand, ADSK would not have recovered 25% from the September low alongside peers.
findings.independence: SEC 8-K exhibit 99.1 of the same release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001031308/000103130826000032/a26q3exhibit991.htm): same document.

findings.finding: Trimble (Q3 reported Nov 4): AECO ARR a record $1.636bn, +13%, AECO revenue +9%, but total organic ARR growth outlook cut to 10% (from 12-14%), partly a $20m white-label shift and weaker positioning/transportation; EPS guide slightly raised.
findings.link: AECO software peer (Tekla, SketchUp, Viewpoint vs Revit, ACC); AECO is ~65% of Trimble ARR; overlapping construction customers.
findings.why_not_priced: Mixed: the AECO line, which overlaps ADSK, is healthy; the cut is in non-overlapping lines. Net close to zero.

findings.finding: Nemetschek (Q3 reported ~Nov 5) grew organic constant-currency revenue 12.5%, below its reaffirmed 14-15% full-year target, with a slower subscription transition in its Design segment; the shares fell more than 8%.
findings.link: Direct competitor in building design (Graphisoft/Vectorworks/Allplan vs Revit/AutoCAD), heavy in Western Europe, the region where ADSK said new-business productivity recovers slowest.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not specific; Western Europe was ADSK's laggard on the Q2 call.
findings.why_not_priced: Read-through on European design demand; ADSK held its range after it, so either discounted or not transmitted. Organic growth below target at a Europe-heavy design peer is a real negative signal for ADSK's Western Europe line, which is a minority of revenue.

findings.finding: AIA/Deltek Architecture Billings Index read 44.9 for October 2026 (44.7 September), more than four years without sustained growth; inquiries rose but newly signed design contracts kept declining.
findings.link: Architects are core Revit/AutoCAD seat buyers within AECO; macro proxy, not confirmed by ADSK, which grew AECO 17% in Q2 through the same weak ABI.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ABI has been below 50 through every ADSK print in the baseline, including the +9.09% and +5.32% ones.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy; ADSK's subscription revenue has decoupled from ABI for years. Filed small.

findings.finding: Autodesk raised FY27 revenue guidance at both prior prints (May: to $8,155-8,215m; August: underlying ~2pt billings raise, revenue to $8,295-8,345m incl. MaintainX) and beat the top of the Q2 revenue guide by ~$30m; a Q3 beat of similar size would support a further revenue/billings raise in the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue raises in May and August were sold (-4.0%, -3.67%) because EPS did not follow; Nov 2025 Q3 raise bought +2.36%.
findings.why_not_priced: A raise is the base case; what is not priced is whether EPS follows. Filed small and positive because the Q3 quarter is where ADSK raised and was bought last year.
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 release (https://finviz.com/news/357930/autodesk-inc-announces-fiscal-2027-first-quarter-results) records the May raise; Jefferies checks above company forecasts.

findings.finding: Management said on the Q2 call that the new transaction model added ~2pts to Q2 revenue growth and ~1.5pts to FY27 and will not recur, that FY28 revenue and FCF are 'too early' to frame, and only that FY28 non-GAAP margin improves modestly from 39% despite a full year of MaintainX costs; a first FY28 framework on this call would show the lift dropping out.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance lines decided the last two reactions (-4.0%, -3.67%).
findings.why_not_priced: Known from August (Trefis framed it on Sep 10), but no FY28 street figure was found, so the bar is unknown; a framework implying low-teens organic growth would land on a stock rallied 25%. Whether ADSK gives FY28 colour in Q3 is not established.
findings.independence: Trefis 2026-09-10 (https://www.trefis.com/articles/614900/why-did-autodesk-stock-drop-so-soon-after-raising-its-forecast/2026-09-10) reads the same comments; same underlying statement.

findings.finding: Billings lagged revenue in Q2 FY27 (billings +10% reported/+12% cc vs revenue +16%/+14% cc), cRPO growth slowed to 12% from 18-20%, total RPO +2% on reduced multiyear discounts; billings are the line the stock is now judged on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 billings/cRPO deceleration accompanied the -3.67% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Public numbers; filed because the comparison in Q3 is the question. The company attributes the RPO drag to multiyear wind-down and calls it temporary.
findings.independence: SiliconANGLE Q2 coverage with RPO $7.433bn +2%, cRPO $5.245bn +12% (https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/27/autodesk-shares-fall-despite-q2-beat-as-cash-flow-guidance-narrows/).

findings.finding: Q2 FY27 buyback was ~2.1m shares for $453m ($901m in H1); FY27 repurchase dollars guided equal to FY26 and ~50% of FCF; the stock traded near $206-230 for much of fiscal Q3, so the Q3 share count likely fell further.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not a reaction line for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Within guided capital return; inside the EPS guide. Small.
findings.independence: Q2 release cash-flow statement ($901m six-month repurchases) (https://finviz.com/news/386371/autodesk-inc-announces-fiscal-2027-second-quarter-results).

findings.finding: Short interest 9.2m shares (4.4% of shares outstanding), 6.1 days to cover, up 130.5k shares at the 2026-11-13 settlement; skew +1.88 vol points, put/call OI 0.93.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price; mildly rising shorts and a mild put premium say a modest bearish tilt with no squeeze setup either way. Snippet-level data.
findings.independence: MarketWatch quote page listed the same 9.2m / 6.1 days with a different settlement date (snippet); AltIndex 9.38m / 4.57 days (https://altindex.com/ticker/adsk/short-interest).

findings.finding: FY27 carries Autodesk's largest-ever EBA renewal cohort, concentrated in Q4, while last year's largest cohort was product subscriptions, making H2 billings comparisons harder; Western Europe new-business productivity was recovering slowest after the sales reorganization.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Billings-quality commentary accompanied the August selloff.
findings.why_not_priced: Management disclosed it; the risk is that a Q4 EBA-heavy guide keeps billings and FCF guide unraised. Shares a document with the FY28 finding but a different line (Q4 billings vs FY28 growth).
findings.independence: Trefis 2026-11-16 names Q4 EBA renewals and Western Europe as the items to watch (https://www.trefis.com/stock/adsk/articles2/625194/how-much-should-one-lagging-number-worry-autodesk-stock-holders/2026-11-16).

findings.finding: MaintainX (closed Aug 3, ~$3.6bn cash) adds ~$60m revenue and ~$70m billings in H2, slightly Q4-weighted, and is reported separately for four quarters, so Q3 is the first print where organic growth can be read net of it; it dilutes margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First print with the acquisition; no history.
findings.why_not_priced: The separate disclosure removes the cover for a soft core; ~$28-30m in Q3 is ~1.4% of revenue, so a headline beat smaller than that is an organic miss of the guide's spirit. Either direction.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript gives the $60m/$70m H2 figures (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262137253-tradingkey).

findings.finding: PTC (fiscal Q4 to Sep 30, reported Nov 4) grew ARR ex-divested businesses 8% (9.7% cc) to ~$2.51bn and beat EPS ($2.03 vs $2.00); it no longer guides because of the pending $22.6bn Schneider Electric takeover announced Oct 5.
findings.link: Manufacturing design/PLM peer (Creo/Onshape vs Fusion/Inventor) in ADSK's Make/manufacturing line (Make revenue $244m in Q2, ~12% of total); the takeover also marks a private-market valuation for design software.
findings.why_not_priced: Steady manufacturing demand signal, small and partly priced.

baseline_tension: The options price an 8.2% move with a balanced skew (+1.88); what was found agrees with that: supportive counterparties and checks against a raised real bar after a 25% rally and a guide pattern the market has sold twice, so no direction beats the skew.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its last two beats): Jefferies field checks +0.8 -> +0.5 and Procore read-through +0.8 -> +0.6, both reported-quarter items.
Core step 4 (apply each lesson once): the 'last two prints sold' finding cut -0.5 -> -0.3, because the same reaction pattern already shrank the two reported-quarter positives.

Lessons 6 and 7 changed nothing: the bar is sourced to the company guide plus an agreeing consensus, the short is not crowded (4.4%, 6.1 days), and the skew is mild. p_up and abs_move_pct are unchanged.
